cim: Structured Prompting Boosts Artificial Intelligence Performance in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Evaluations
cim_eredeti: Structured Prompting Boosts Artificial Intelligence Performance in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Evaluations
szoveg_eredeti:
Structured Prompting Boosts Artificial Intelligence Performance in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Evaluations

A blinded comparative study evaluating artificial intelligence systems across the continuum of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis care has found that structured reasoning prompts significantly improve clinician-rated response quality over standard zero-shot instructions, though differences between advanced reasoning frameworks remained statistically indistinguishable. The investigation, published in Frontiers in Digital Health by clinical researchers from Sun Yat-sen University and computer scientists from Shenzhen University, systematically tested six mainstream large language models across four distinct clinical stages: prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. Using randomized evaluations performed by six rehabilitation medicine specialists across five clinical competency domains, the researchers observed that models guided by structured reasoning pathways achieved higher composite ratings than models answering without explicit guidance. Across the entire test battery, the tested systems generated overall mean composite scores ranging from 4.35 to 4.69 on a five-point scale, demonstrating generally acceptable response quality on simulated consultations while displaying pronounced domain-specific and stage-dependent performance boundaries that caution against unmonitored clinical adoption.

Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis represents the most prevalent three-dimensional spinal deformity observed in adolescents between 10 and 18 years of age, affecting an estimated 2 to 3 percent of this population. The condition does not arise from an isolated cause; instead, current evidence implicates a complex interplay among genetic susceptibility, abnormal regulation of physical growth and development, and biomechanical environmental forces. While a substantial proportion of affected adolescents do not exhibit conspicuous symptoms initially, progressive spinal curvature can lead to visible physical appearance abnormalities, impaired pulmonary function, and long-term deteriorations in overall quality of life. Clinical management depends heavily on classification systems such as the Lenke taxonomy, which stratifies structural subtypes alongside the Cobb angle, Risser sign, and physical markers to guide conservative brace selection, specialized physical therapy, surgical timing, and long-term prognosis. However, specialized orthopedic and rehabilitation resources remain geographically and socioeconomically constrained, leaving patients in resource-limited settings vulnerable to diagnostic delays and fragmented care. Generative language models have consequently emerged as potential scalable adjuncts for home-based guidance, brace adherence support, and family education.

To evaluate whether generative systems can reliably address the diverse challenges of scoliosis management, the investigators designed twenty representative consultation questions anchored in real-world clinical encounters. All questions were framed from the perspective of parents caring for an affected child named Lily, mirroring common caregiver concerns regarding daily posture, diagnostic screening, brace compliance, and progression anxiety. The prevention scenario detailed a twelve-year-old girl who habitually slouched during homework, carried her school bag over one shoulder, and avoided physical activity, prompting parental inquiries regarding proactive lifestyle modifications. The diagnostic stage examined asymmetrical shoulder heights and back protrusion detected during school-based physical screenings. The treatment scenario addressed parental distress following a confirmed diagnosis involving a thirty-degree Cobb angle, where conservative bracing and exercise were prescribed amidst fears of social ridicule. Finally, the prognostic scenario addressed persistent parental apprehension regarding spinal curve progression and potential surgical intervention despite ongoing conservative compliance. Each stage contained five contextualized questions vetted by rehabilitation physicians and spine surgery specialists.

The experimental protocol tested six commercial and open-weight model architectures retrieved on April 13, 2026: Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview, GPT-5-Pro, Claude-Sonnet-4-6-Thinking, GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-Reasoner, and Qwen-Max. Each platform was accessed through official application programming interfaces operating under native reasoning modes with provider-default sampling temperatures, top-p thresholds, and computational reasoning budgets. No external web-browsing tools or retrieval-augmented systems were permitted, ensuring outputs reflected only intrinsic model knowledge and prompting constraints. Each model generated answers under three distinct prompt engineering strategies: zero-shot learning, which solicited answers without task-specific demonstrations or reasoning scaffolding; chain-of-thought prompting, which directed the model to articulate stepwise linear reasoning; and tree-of-thought prompting, which instructed the system to execute exploratory, multi-branching deliberative analysis. Every question, model, and prompting combination was generated as an independent single-turn interaction separated by a one-second interval, yielding a standardized corpus of 360 unique clinical responses without repeated sampling or post-hoc response selection.

Response evaluation was conducted through a purpose-built online platform that presented anonymized, randomized outputs to six rehabilitation medicine specialists blinded to model identities and prompting configurations. The assessment rubric encompassed five dimensions defined on a five-point Likert scale: clinical applicability and safety, scientific rigor and evidence-based grounding, individualization and clinical problem-solving, empathy and humanistic care, and clarity and logical coherence. To analyze the resulting 2,160 individual ratings per domain, the investigators fitted pooled linear mixed-effects models via restricted maximum likelihood, specifying fixed effects for model architecture, prompting strategy, and clinical stage, while incorporating crossed random intercepts for evaluators alongside nested intercepts for specific questions and individual responses. Statistical significance was defined using two-sided tests adjusted for multiple comparisons through the Holm-Bonferroni correction, while uncertainty was characterized using 95 percent Wald confidence intervals. Inter-rater reliability was measured using two-way random-effects intraclass correlation coefficients and Kendall rank concordance.

Across the evaluated models, observed mean composite scores averaged across all five clinical dimensions ranged from 4.35 to 4.69 points. Gemini achieved the highest numerical composite average at 4.69, closely followed by GPT-5 at 4.62 and Claude at 4.61, with GLM recording 4.50, DeepSeek 4.38, and Qwen 4.35. In linear mixed-effects comparisons using GPT-5 as the reference baseline, neither Gemini nor Claude demonstrated statistically significant differences in composite performance after Holm adjustment, with an adjusted mean difference of 0.07 points for Gemini and negative 0.01 points for Claude. Conversely, GLM, DeepSeek, and Qwen exhibited statistically significant performance deficits relative to GPT-5, showing mean differences of negative 0.12, negative 0.24, and negative 0.27 points, respectively. Domain-level decompositions demonstrated that GPT-5 achieved the highest observed rating in scientific rigor at 4.65 points, while Gemini led observed scores in safety at 4.72, individualization at 4.67, and clarity at 4.76 points, though differences between top-tier models were largely nonsignificant.
